name: MonitorObject
summary: Serializes concurrent method calls on an object so that only one runs at a time, and lets its methods cooperatively schedule their turns.

reference.author: Douglas Schmidt, Michael Stal, Hans Rohnert, Frank Buschmann

roles.name: MonitorObject
roles.summary: The object whose methods are serialized. It has no thread of its own: every method runs in the thread of the client that called it, which is the whole difference from an active object and the reason a long method here blocks a caller rather than a worker.

roles.name: SynchronizedMethod
roles.summary: One of the thread-safe services the monitor exports. Exactly one of them runs inside the monitor at a time, whatever the number of threads calling and whatever the number of such methods — so the object's throughput is one method, not one per caller.

roles.name: MonitorLock
roles.summary: The lock this monitor object holds of its own, taken as a synchronized method enters and released as it leaves. One monitor object, one lock: sharing a lock between two of them serializes both and neither of them says so.

roles.name: MonitorCondition
roles.summary: What a synchronized method waits on when it cannot make progress, which releases the monitor lock and suspends the caller until another method notifies it. A condition nothing ever notifies is a caller that never returns, and no compiler pairs the two.
